title: Episode 21: A Handful of Youtube Channels to Enjoy
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FlbiS6qn6oE

Daniel (@dungeondive) hands the microphone to other people's channels, and the selection criterion is openly stated: he wants lo-fi. Unscripted, minimally edited, someone setting a camera down and talking — several of these look shot on an eighties camcorder, which he means as praise. Almost all sit under 5,000 subscribers.

The one video-game entry, **The Metroidvania Review**, comes with a melancholy note: its author posted a farewell in October 2021 citing burnout and no payoff, though a tier list of hundreds of Metroidvanias has since resumed. **Artichoke Dip** was among the first channels he watched, and its solo RPG introduction is where he first met the format he now covers constantly. **Battlin' Barrow Gaming** builds convincing terrain cheaply. **Catweasel** does playthroughs of precisely the games this audience likes — *Eldritch Horror*, *Perdition's Mouth*, *Secrets of the Lost Tomb*. **Danisch** is excellent and entirely in German, which Daniel doesn't speak. **Stone Axe Tabletop Gaming**, **Solo Adventures with Livy** and **Magehammer's Gametable** round it out.

He interrupts his own episode mid-recording — having already uploaded and pulled it — to splice in **The Solo RPG Guy**, forgotten on the first pass.

----

What does a channel gain from staying lo-fi, and at what point does production polish start costing something?
